First preview release of **EatPoint**, a fork of [OpenNutriTracker](https://github.com/simonoppowa/OpenNutriTracker) that adds a points system, a nutrition-label scanner, weekly menus with a joint shopping list, household sync and an agent connector.

> **Preview build.** EatPoint installs as a separate app (`io.github.grohle.eatpoint`) next to OpenNutriTracker; it does not read the other app's data. To bring your diary over, export it from OpenNutriTracker (Settings → Export) and import it in EatPoint.

## What's new

**Points (1 point = 100 kcal of one macronutrient)**
- Every food shows its points per 100 g and how they split between carbs, protein and fat.
- When you log a food, the grams and points fields stay in sync. Typing points fills in practical grams for a kitchen scale (to 1 g under 30 g, 5 g up to 150 g, 10 g above), and you can step by quarter points.
- Each meal has its own carbs/protein/fat budget, and the amount sheet shows how the serving fits it.
- Home shows a points ring with per-macro and per-meal usage. The original calorie view is one tap away.
- Suggested daily budget: lean mass (protein first, rest split between carbs and fat) by default, or the app's own calorie goal and macros. It's labelled as **a guide only**, and every number is editable.

**Nutrition-label scanner**
- Photograph a label to fill in a custom food. On-device text recognition reads the per-100 g values in Spanish and English and checks the calories against the macros.
- A review screen sits beside the photo, so you can correct any value before saving.
- Optional retry with the AI provider you configured for AI assistance. It always asks before a photo is sent.

**Weekly menu and shopping list**
- Plan the week from dishes you have logged or saved before, sorted by how well they fit the points left.
- Log a planned meal in one tap. Copy the previous week, or copy a day to other days.
- The shopping list adds up the week's menus by ingredient, expands recipes into their ingredients and groups items by aisle. Tick items off, add your own, share as text or export as CSV.
- Optional local reminders to plan the week, do the shopping, prepare tomorrow's food and log what you planned.

**Shared household (end-to-end encrypted)**
- Link two phones with a QR code shown in person. You see each other's menu next to yours, and the joint shopping list syncs ticks between phones.
- Storage options:
  - your own Supabase project (the app can create the database for you);
  - a Nextcloud/WebDAV folder;
  - your own Ubuntu server, where the app installs a small sync service over SSH.
- The storage only ever holds AES-256-GCM ciphertext.

**Agent connector (MCP)**
- An MCP server runs on the phone while the app is open, so any MCP client on your Wi‑Fi can read your budget, menus, shopping list and dishes.
- Agents can only *propose* changes, which you approve in the app. The diary stays private unless you allow it.

**Also**
- Complete English and Spanish.
- Export and import EatPoint data as JSON.
- New name, logo and launcher icons.

## Coming next
- **On-device AI model for labels:** an optional download that reads difficult labels offline.
- **More scripts and alphabets in the label scanner:** Chinese, Japanese, Korean and Devanagari, and Cyrillic, Greek and Arabic labels. This build reads Latin-script labels.
- **Google Drive** storage for the household.

## Downloads
- `EatPoint-0.1.0-arm64-v8a.apk` (57 MB): for almost every phone from the last few years.
- `EatPoint-0.1.0-universal.apk` (146 MB): for any Android 8.0+ device.

## Known limitations of this build
- **Online food database:** OpenNutriTracker's database (USDA/BLS) is not configured in this build. Food search uses Open Food Facts, your custom foods and your recipes.
- **Crash reporting** is disabled.
- **Tip jar:** the upstream tip jar is shown but has no products for this app id.
- **Agent connector:** it only runs while the app is in the foreground.
